A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPDreamer. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, and equations, support reliable comparison despite changes in title, organization, and layout.

before.justification: v3 reports original 3D-generation experiments, FID and CLIP scores, an 80-person preference study, and geometry and texture ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons, CLIP scores, and user preferences evaluating LEPI.

M1.justification: v4 introduces optional Local Editing with Partial Images (LEPI). It uses partial image prompts and localization words to construct spatially masked attention, followed by global texture optimization using combined prompt features. This substantially extends the procedure beyond v3's global image-prompt guidance; the original NeRF and IPSD components remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-3D generation, single-image-to-3D generation, and complex-image-guided texture editing. Severe prompt–NeRF mismatch was already tested in v3's failed doll example. The additional LEPI examples and single-image example extend results within this coverage without introducing a distinct task or dataset.

E2.justification: The new LEPI comparisons explicitly use IPDreamer without LEPI as an internal comparator, including Table 5 and Figures 3, 7, and 10. External comparator membership remains unchanged: DreamFusion, Magic3D, Fantasia3D, and ProlificDreamer for text-to-3D, and Zero-1-to-3 and SyncDreamer for the corresponding image-based comparisons.

E3.justification: v4 adds a paired with/without-LEPI evaluation using image prompts from Figures 3, 7, 10, and 11, assessed through CLIP scores and user preferences. The original 20-prompt benchmark, 80-volunteer study with 1,280 comparisons, and stated optimization budgets remain unchanged. LEPI-specific participant and trial counts are not separately specified.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantial evidence testing whether LEPI preserves object semantics under strong appearance mismatch: the revisited doll failure, bird and cottage ablations, additional controlled examples, quantitative comparisons, and localization-mask visualization. The existing geometry-loss, geometry-prompt-difference, and combined-supervision analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed evaluations, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. v4's additional CLIP scores and preference percentages follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds a substantial block of LEPI findings. Table 5 reports CLIP scores of 0.2041 without LEPI and 0.2189 with LEPI, with preference rates of 24.363% and 75.637%, respectively. New qualitative comparisons demonstrate improved semantic preservation, and Figure 14 adds a single-image example. The original benchmark, baseline-preference, and geometry-prompt ablation numbers are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 substantially extends the mathematical formulation with localization-mask and masked-attention definitions in Equations 10–11 and local/global LEPI supervision in Equations 15–21. Core IPSD and combined Zero-1-to-3 supervision equations are retained. v3's preliminary VSD optimization equations are removed. Neither version provides formal guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v4 adds LEPI as an explicit principal contribution, claiming successful editing when image prompts differ substantially from the initial NeRF. This extends the contribution beyond v3's IPSD framework and general controllable-generation claims. The central claims concerning high-quality, appearance-controllable 3D synthesis remain.

C2.justification: v4 explains complex-image guidance through attention-based spatial alignment and attributes severe-mismatch failures to inadequate localization. LEPI is presented as addressing that mechanism. The limitations discussion changes from v3's demonstrated doll-editing failure and incomplete style control to residual appearance/color inconsistency and deployment speed.

D1.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a substantial implementation workflow: GPT-4v analysis, SAM segmentation, user-adjustable partial prompts, ControlNet enhancement with a specified checkpoint, and local followed by global optimization. Existing hardware, iteration counts, timestep schedules, memory requirements, and code access remain unchanged. However, v3's explicit several-hours-per-model runtime description disappears.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including Prompt-to-Prompt, Segment Anything, DreamGaussian, LucidDreamer, and newer image/video diffusion work. Related work expands to Gaussian-based 3D optimization and additional editing methods, while the main positioning against text-to-3D and single-image-to-3D approaches remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized around LEPI. The original user study, single-image generation, and Zero-1-to-3 comparison move into expanded appendices; attention explanation enters the main method section, and VSD preliminaries are shortened. The introduction, contribution list, limitations, title, and author block are also revised.

P2.justification: v4 changes the page format and extensively rearranges displays. It redraws the teaser and pipeline, transposes Table 1, adds LEPI comparison figures, a mask visualization, and Table 5, and relocates several retained figures. The original standalone optimization illustration and teaser's dragon panels are omitted; the doll failure is reused within a new controlled comparison.

improvement.justification: v4 materially addresses a demonstrated weakness in the paper's central controllability goal: v3's failed doll edit becomes a controlled LEPI comparison in Figure 3, supported by further ablations and Table 5. The added mechanism explanation and implementation workflow strengthen this evidence. LEPI-specific study details and uncertainty reporting remain limited, and runtime disclosure is weakened, but the demonstrated mitigation of an important failure makes the overall improvement substantial.
